items.title: Carter Benny — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History
items.q: when Max Roach came into the band

ctx.x: You just mentioned that a lot of people were getting drafted. Was that the only reason these people came in, or did you want to inject a different kind of sound or you were attracted to some of these younger musicians?

No, but, I mean, some of those I replaced because they went into the service. But, no, I don’t know. Just, you know, J. J. Johnson joined me in Indianapolis [Indiana] and came to California with me. Now, when Max Roach came into the band, I don’t remember. Miles Davis was in the band in ’46, something, and he was with it for just a short time, maybe a matter of weeks.
You picked him up in St. Louis [Missouri], is that correct?

items.title: 66095_Benny Carter oral history interview
items.q: And Max Roach was with the band, it seems, since about '44, I guess.

ctx.x: And Max Roach was with the band, it seems, since about '44, I guess. Yeah. Freddie Webster about '44, and ...

I think I know your answer to this, but I'm gonna ask it anyway -- did you feel that these guys were playing something new that you wanted to have part of your band, or were you again, just picking up good musicians, playing good music or whatever it was?
